I need to evaluate the claim that Bodhidharma is described as "The Blue-Eyed Barbarian" in Chinese texts.

Bodhidharma was indeed a Buddhist monk who lived around the 5th-6th century CE and is credited with transmitting Chan Buddhism (Zen) to China. Historical and legendary accounts describe him as coming from either India or Persia/Central Asia.

In Chinese texts, Bodhidharma is frequently referred to as "碧眼胡" (bìyǎn hú), which translates to "blue-eyed barbarian" or "green-eyed barbarian."
